result.title: MSBench: Benchmarking Script-Controlled Multi-Shot Text-to-Video Generation
result.summary: Text-to-video (T2V) models can now generate visually plausible short clips, but multi-shot generation requires a different set of skills: composing multiple shots with intended cut timing, transition style, camera language, and cross-shot continuity. How far this multi-shot output can be controlled from text remains unmeasured: existing benchmarks either evaluate single shots or, when they provide shot-level scripts, typically check whether the requested shots appear but not when they change or how they are joined. We introduce MSBench, a benchmark for controllable text-driven multi-shot video generation built around structured Scene-Entity-Shot mini-scripts that specify each shot's time span, camera state, content, and outgoing transition. MSBench defines a four-dimensional hybrid evaluation framework spanning Visual Quality, Dynamic Quality, Semantic Alignment, and Cross-Shot Consistency with 11 sub-metrics. Experiments on 14 commercial and open-source systems show that visual quality does little to separate the systems, whereas multi-shot control does: many models cut mainly on scene changes and render requested gradual transitions as hard cuts. Human evaluations further validate MSBench, with its system ranking reaching a Spearman correlation of 0.87 with human preferences. The project page is available at https://totalhuang.github.io/MSBench-page/.
